parts.title: Part I — Clinical Presentation
parts.blurb: What ME/CFS is, how it presents, and how it is diagnosed and classified.

chapters.title: Introduction to ME/CFS
chapters.about: Introduces ME/CFS as a complex, chronic, multi-system disease marked by disabling fatigue, post-exertional malaise, unrefreshing sleep, cognitive dysfunction, and autonomic dysregulation. Covers recognition by major health organizations (WHO ICD-11 code 8E49, CDC, NIH), estimated global prevalence of 0.89–2.5%, and the evolving terminology debate between “chronic fatigue syndrome” and “myalgic encephalomyelitis.”

chapters.title: History of ME/CFS
chapters.about: A chronological account of the disease from the 1934 Los Angeles County Hospital outbreak, the Iceland/Akureyri outbreak, and the 1955 Royal Free epidemic through Acheson’s 1959 synthesis of 14 epidemics. Traces the shift from psychosomatic to biological framing across the PACE trial controversy, the 2015 IOM redefinition, and the 2024 NIH deep phenotyping study.

chapters.title: Core Symptoms
chapters.about: Opens the core-symptom discussion by focusing on fatigue, the most prevalent and severe symptom, distinguished from fatigability. Covers its definition, a quantitative severity benchmark (about 78/100 from a pooled meta-analysis of 60 RCTs), objective measurement via actigraphy and neuroimaging pointing to a central neural origin, and evidence that fatigue is a cross-cutting feature within multi-system symptom clusters rather than a unitary construct.

chapters.title: Additional Symptoms and Manifestations
chapters.about: Catalogs the additional symptoms beyond the core set, organized by manifestation: sensory sensitivities (photophobia, hyperacusis, allodynia, chemical and odor sensitivities), motor and coordination symptoms, paresthesias, dizziness and vertigo, dysautonomia, tinnitus, and non-epileptic seizure-like episodes. Extends across immune, musculoskeletal, gastrointestinal, cardiovascular, respiratory, genitourinary, endocrine, ocular, auditory, psychological, and sleep-related symptoms.

chapters.title: Diagnostic Criteria and Clinical Assessment
chapters.about: Reviews the major ME/CFS diagnostic frameworks, noting that diagnosis remains clinical in the absence of a definitive test. Traces the evolution from early frameworks (Holmes 1988, Fukuda 1994) through restrictive ones (Canadian Consensus 2003, ICC 2011) to the IOM criteria of 2015, presents a set-theoretic comparison showing a partial ordering by restrictiveness, and examines the specificity-versus-homogeneity trade-off.

chapters.title: Disease Course and Prognosis
chapters.about: Examines how ME/CFS begins: acute post-infectious onset (roughly 64% of cases, with EBV, SARS-CoV-2, influenza, and enteroviruses among documented triggers) versus gradual onset, plus two-phase, multi-hit cascade, and bimodal onset patterns. Covers retrospective prodromal signs, evidence for two onset-age peaks near ages 16 and 37, and how early-onset disease carries higher severity and greater familial clustering.

parts.title: Part II — Pathophysiology
parts.blurb: The biological mechanisms and multi-system dysfunctions underlying ME/CFS.

chapters.title: Energy Metabolism and Mitochondrial Function
chapters.about: Covers cellular energy metabolism as a ten-step chain from substrate delivery to ATP utilization, with glucose-basis ATP accounting for each step. Reviews glycolysis, the Krebs cycle, and the electron transport chain, evidence for mitochondrial impairment across measurement modalities, the 2024 NIH Walitt study metabolomics, and four integrative hypotheses linking multiple steps.

chapters.title: Immune System Dysfunction
chapters.about: Examines immune dysfunction across the innate and adaptive systems, inflammatory mediators, and potential autoimmune mechanisms. Details Natural Killer cell dysfunction, viral persistence and clearance failure hypotheses, TRPM3 ion channel dysfunction, neutrophil and monocyte function including NETosis, and proposes upstream mechanisms such as MDSC expansion and arginine depletion.

chapters.title: Neurological and Neurocognitive Dysfunction
chapters.about: Covers central nervous system dysfunction, including structural and functional neuroimaging findings, PET hypometabolism, SPECT perfusion abnormalities, cerebral blood flow findings during orthostatic challenge, and neurotransmitter abnormalities including CSF catecholamine deficiency and tryptophan/kynurenine pathway alterations. Proposes a brain-centric model of energy coordination.

chapters.title: Endocrine and Metabolic Dysfunction
chapters.about: Examines six major endocrine systems implicated in ME/CFS: HPA axis dysfunction with blunted cortisol, low T3 syndrome, sex hormone dysregulation, growth hormone and IGF-1 deficiencies, insulin resistance with cerebral glucose hypometabolism, and circadian rhythm disruption. Also covers post-viral pituitary injury and secondary adrenal insufficiency.

chapters.title: Cardiovascular Dysfunction
chapters.about: Covers cardiovascular abnormalities centered on cardiopulmonary exercise testing findings (reduced peak VO2, chronotropic incompetence, two-day CPET post-exertional decline). Details cardiac output and stroke volume deficits, preload failure, reduced blood volume, venous pooling, cardiac biomarkers, and GPCR autoantibody-driven autonomic dysfunction.

chapters.title: Gastrointestinal and Microbiome Dysfunction
chapters.about: Examines gastrointestinal symptoms and the gut microbiome, covering dysbiosis patterns, deficient butyrate-producing capacity, multi-omic integration, tryptophan metabolism alterations, the gut-brain axis including the enterochromaffin-vagal serotonergic pathway, intestinal permeability and bacterial translocation, mast cell interactions, and tissue-resident T cell dysfunction.

chapters.title: Brain Clearance Architecture
chapters.about: Addresses the glymphatic system, meningeal lymphatics, and brain clearance in ME/CFS, including the nearest-exit architecture, dual-speed glymphatics, the PEM ratchet, and CSF:blood ratio biomarkers. Covers the sleep-dependent coupling that links clearance to non-REM slow-wave activity.

chapters.title: Genetic and Epigenetic Factors
chapters.about: Covers the genetic architecture and epigenetic modifications underlying susceptibility. Details heritability evidence from twin and family studies, candidate gene studies, and genome-wide association findings, especially the DecodeME GWAS identifying eight significant loci, SNP heritability, genetic correlations with other conditions, polygenic risk scores, and the mitophagy vulnerability hypothesis.

chapters.title: Integrative Models and Multi-System Pathophysiology
chapters.about: Synthesizes the multi-system pathophysiology into comprehensive models, arguing that individual system abnormalities co-occur in coordinated, self-reinforcing patterns rather than independent parallel pathology. Establishes an evidence-level classification and examines unifying mechanisms across systems.

chapters.title: Comparative Nosology: ME/CFS Among Contested Diagnoses
chapters.about: Systematically compares ME/CFS with fibromyalgia, irritable bowel syndrome, post-treatment Lyme disease, complex regional pain syndrome, Gulf War illness, mast cell activation syndrome, Ehlers-Danlos/hypermobility, Long COVID, and other post-infectious fatigue syndromes. Examines diagnostic boundary disputes, shared mechanisms, and the splitting-versus-lumping debate.

chapters.title: Speculative Mechanistic Hypotheses
chapters.about: Presents speculative, not-yet-validated hypotheses about pathogenesis derived from creative extrapolation of known biochemistry and systems biology. Organizes hypotheses into categories (CPET-derived, core mechanistic, autoimmune/immune, viral/cellular, metabolic compartmentalization, integrated, cycle dynamics, high-risk), each ranked by evidence level and therapeutic potential.

chapters.title: Symptom-Producing Mechanisms in ME/CFS
chapters.about: Distinguishes capacity-limiting mechanisms from symptom-producing mechanisms that generate the lived experience of fatigue, cognitive impairment, pain, and malaise. Traces symptom production from integrative frameworks like sickness behavior through specific neurochemical generators into systems-level amplifiers such as glymphatic failure and central sensitization.

chapters.title: Causal Hierarchy: Root Causes, Amplifiers, and Consequences
chapters.about: Proposes a three-tier classification distinguishing trigger-capable root causes, amplifiers, and downstream consequences. Establishes four discriminating criteria (precipitant compatibility, energy collapse sufficiency, chronicity, multi-system spread) and argues from genetic evidence that constitutional vulnerability maps to neuronal circuits.

chapters.title: ME/CFS Through the Lens of Universal Disease Mechanisms
chapters.about: Surveys a taxonomy of roughly 19 universal disease mechanism families and assesses where ME/CFS stands within each, from energy and redox regulation through immune activation, autonomic, neuroendocrine, viral persistence, and purinergic/danger signalling. For each family it enumerates concrete mechanisms, the state of ME/CFS-specific evidence, and cross-references the chapter treating it in depth.

parts.title: Part III — Treatment
parts.blurb: How ME/CFS is treated across severity levels and therapeutic domains.

chapters.title: Mechanism–Treatment Map
chapters.about: The navigational entry point to Part III, answering for each known mechanism what treatment options exist. Organizes treatments by causal tier (trigger-capable root causes versus amplifier mechanisms) and presents a one-page overview table with therapeutic priority ratings and an intervention count per mechanism, along with coverage gaps.

chapters.title: Symptom-Based Management
chapters.about: Addresses what can be done about each symptom now, organized by symptom domain rather than drug class or mechanism. Opens with comorbidity management and covers post-exertional malaise, sleep, pain, cognitive dysfunction, orthostatic intolerance, and broader autonomic symptoms, pairing non-pharmacological and pharmacological options with stated evidence strength.

chapters.title: Urgent Action Plan for Severe Cases
chapters.about: Addresses patients with severe, unbearable suffering, arguing that immediate aggressive symptom management is justified. Presents an honest assessment of severe disease prognosis and grounds its multi-system targeting approach (mast cells, autonomic/cardiovascular function, sleep, metabolic state, immune activation) in a mechanistic vicious-cycle framework.

chapters.title: Action Plans for Mild to Moderate Cases
chapters.about: Addresses patients with mild to moderate ME/CFS who retain some functional capacity, aiming to maximize function, prevent progression to severe disease, and pursue recovery. Draws on pediatric recovery rates versus adult disease to argue for treating early and aggressively and preventing severe crashes.

chapters.title: Pediatric ME/CFS: Severe and Housebound Cases
chapters.about: Addresses the roughly 5–10% of pediatric patients who are housebound or bedbound, providing guidance for home-based care, medical management with pediatric dosing, and strategies to preserve developmental progress. Contrasts pediatric severe disease with adult severe disease and details management including pediatric mast cell activation syndrome treatment.

chapters.title: Pediatric ME/CFS: School-Attending and Ambulatory Cases
chapters.about: Addresses ambulatory pediatric patients who can attend school at least part-time, arguing that early intervention is critical because appropriate management may preserve the window for recovery while inappropriate management risks progression to severe disease. Details the costs of delayed or inappropriate intervention.

chapters.title: Medications Targeting Underlying Mechanisms
chapters.about: Reviews medications that target underlying mechanisms, with substantial coverage of low-dose naltrexone (LDN): proposed mechanisms, dosing protocols, evidence, and a detailed medication-differential analysis of what a response or non-response reveals. Also touches on immunoglobulins, rituximab, and other immunomodulators.

chapters.title: Supplements and Nutraceuticals
chapters.about: Reviews commonly used supplements and nutraceuticals, emphasizing accessible over-the-counter options while being honest about the limited evidence base. Focuses substantially on electrolyte and fluid management for autonomic dysfunction, covering sodium, potassium, magnesium, complete electrolyte formulas, and oral rehydration solutions.

chapters.title: Lifestyle and Non-Pharmacological Interventions
chapters.about: Covers non-pharmacological interventions centered on pacing as the most evidence-based approach, grounded in energy envelope theory and validated by two-day cardiopulmonary exercise testing. Covers heart rate monitoring, avoiding boom-bust cycles, cognitive pacing, and caregiver-implemented pacing for severe patients.

chapters.title: Emerging and Investigational Therapies
chapters.about: Surveys emerging and investigational therapies identified through novel immunophenotyping, cross-disease mechanistic inference, and targeted pathway intervention, none of which have completed randomized controlled trials for ME/CFS. Spans CCR7/CCL19 immune trafficking restoration, checkpoint modulation, BTK inhibition, low-dose IL-2, an emergency PEM prevention protocol, and brain clearance drug targets.

chapters.title: Integrative and Personalized Treatment Approaches
chapters.about: Provides a safety-first framework for treatment planning, arguing that every treatment trial carries a metabolic energy cost and failed trials can trigger post-exertional malaise. Classifies interventions by energy category, establishes a micro-dosing imperative, provides crash-risk rankings, sequencing plans, and when-to-stop criteria.

chapters.title: Medication Response Reference: From Drug Response to Mechanism Identification
chapters.about: Argues that every drug response (therapeutic benefit, null response, or side effect at a specific dose) is diagnostic information, providing frameworks for reading dose-response curves, side-effect patterns, and cross-drug combination signals. Frames the medication-as-probe approach as diagnostic reasoning under uncertainty.

chapters.title: Mechanistic Cascade Tracing: From Hypothesis to Clinical Probe
chapters.about: Traces the full downstream cascade for every major mechanistic hypothesis, from proposed trigger to terminal neurochemical, metabolic, and immunological consequences, identifying at each node which medications could intercept and what a response reveals. Works through the PIP2/TRPM3 channelopathy cascade, TRPV1-mediated vasoconstriction, and Piezo2 dysfunction.

parts.title: Part IV — Research
parts.blurb: The evidence base: methods, biomarkers, trials, epidemiology, and policy.

chapters.title: ME/CFS-Specific Research Methods
chapters.about: Examines the methodological challenges that undermine replicability, centered on case definition heterogeneity, and argues that the choice of diagnostic criteria determines which biology is studied. Discusses PEM as a constraint on participation, the 2-day CPET reliability debate, biomarker overfitting, and statistical power in heterogeneous populations.

chapters.title: Biomarker Research
chapters.about: Reviews the state of biomarker research across biological domains, including why biomarkers are needed, the types of biomarkers, and the challenges complicating their identification. Synthesizes evidence for convergent biology despite heterogeneity and covers machine-learning approaches to EBV-based diagnosis and AI sleep-physiology biomarkers.

chapters.title: Clinical Trials and Treatment Studies
chapters.about: Reviews clinical trial evidence by intervention category with attention to methodological quality. Covers the rituximab program from promising pilot data through the negative RituxME phase III trial, low-dose naltrexone studies, and other immune modulators including IVIG, interferon-alpha, rintatolimod (Ampligen), and immunoadsorption.

chapters.title: Mechanistic and Experimental Studies
chapters.about: Examines the 2024 NIH deep phenotyping study of post-infectious ME/CFS in detail, describing its design, comprehensive assessment battery, and key biological findings across catecholamine deficiency, immune dysfunction, autonomic dysfunction, and neuroimaging. Documents its limitations and the “effort preference” controversy.

chapters.title: Epidemiological and Outcomes Research
chapters.about: Covers the epidemiology of ME/CFS, including population-based prevalence estimates that vary by diagnostic criteria, geographic and demographic variation (sex ratio, bimodal age onset, ethnic and socioeconomic factors), and the post-COVID surge in incidence. Also discusses population-level cognitive impact of COVID and vaccination.

chapters.title: Healthcare Systems, Policy, and Disability
chapters.about: Analyzes how healthcare systems respond to ME/CFS, covering medical education deficits, diagnostic delay and underdiagnosis, specialist clinic models, guideline inconsistencies, insurance and disability benefit systems, and healthcare disparities. Proposes a four-failure model of healthcare-system dysfunction.

chapters.title: Economic Impact of ME/CFS
chapters.about: Quantifies the economic burden of ME/CFS, covering direct costs, indirect costs (lost earnings, reduced workforce participation), caregiver burden, and lifetime cost estimates per patient. Presents the IOM 2015 benchmark, Australian cost-of-illness studies, and Belgian population-level data, and makes the economic case for increased research funding.

chapters.title: Controversies and Debates in ME/CFS Research
chapters.about: Examines the contested naming and terminology of the disease (ME, CFS, ME/CFS, SEID) and how the terminology debate affects research funding, clinical recognition, and patient treatment. Documents how the “chronic fatigue syndrome” label generates more negative attributions and stigma than alternative names.

chapters.title: Translational Findings: Implications for Related Conditions
chapters.about: Identifies mechanisms, biomarkers, and treatment protocols from ME/CFS research that have implications for other post-viral, autoimmune, mitochondrial, and dysautonomic conditions. Presents translational opportunities covering post-viral autoimmunity, autonomic-vascular integration, mitochondrial pathophysiology, neuroinflammation, and exercise intolerance, using a three-tier certainty framework.

chapters.title: Global and Low-Resource Perspectives on ME/CFS
chapters.about: Examines ME/CFS in global and low-resource settings: the hidden post-infectious fatigue burden in high-infectious-disease regions, cultural variation in symptom expression, diagnostic access without specialized testing, ICD classification, traditional medicine approaches, and research priorities. Argues that absent data reflects absent diagnostic infrastructure rather than absence of the disease.

chapters.title: Research Infrastructure Proposals
chapters.about: Proposes foundational research infrastructure centered on the “ME/CFS Human Phenome Project,” a multi-site longitudinal deep phenotyping cohort with comprehensive multi-omic, immune, autonomic, exercise-physiology, and neuroimaging assessment. Details study design, biorepository specifications, data infrastructure, budget, and feasibility.

chapters.title: Patient-Generated Knowledge and Citizen Science
chapters.about: Describes the patient-led research movement in ME/CFS, covering patient organizations that fund research, co-produced study designs like DecodeME, biobanks and registries, n=1 experimentation, and epistemic correction of flawed institutional research such as the FOIA-driven reanalysis of the PACE trial. Applies the epistemic injustice framework.

chapters.title: Proposed Studies
chapters.about: Presents detailed protocols and registry-style entries for proposed research studies testing hypotheses about mechanisms and recovery, each carrying explicit hypotheses, predictions, treatments, and limitations with confidence estimates. Covers viral reactivation, menstrual-cycle pharmacodiagnostic probes, OXPHOS-VO2max uncoupling, PEM characterization, and a multi-modal selective energy dysfunction study protocol.

chapters.title: Consolidated Research Proposals Index
chapters.about: Collects every research proposal scattered across the paper into a single table sorted by impact-weighted feasibility, linking each row to its full protocol or source environment. Spans biomarker-development, secondary-analysis, observational, infrastructure, and interventional proposals.

parts.title: Part V — Quantitative Modeling
parts.blurb: Formal mathematical models of ME/CFS disease dynamics.

chapters.title: Foundations of ME/CFS Modeling
chapters.about: Establishes the mathematical and modeling framework underpinning the specific models in Part V. Explains why formal modeling is needed for ME/CFS (managing multi-system complexity, generating testable predictions, optimizing interventions, enabling personalized medicine), citing the Naviaux hypometabolic state and the energy envelope theory as motivating examples.

chapters.title: Energy Metabolism Models
chapters.about: Translates qualitative understanding of energy metabolism dysfunction into formal mathematical models, progressing from glycolysis kinetics through the Krebs cycle and electron transport chain to an integrated energy production system. Develops ODE models with Michaelis-Menten and Hill-type kinetics, explaining how reduced mitochondrial enzyme activity creates a nonlinear cliff effect.

chapters.title: Immune System Models
chapters.about: Develops mathematical models of the immune subsystems disrupted in ME/CFS, covering NK cell activity, a cytokine network model capturing the pro-inflammatory to remodeled state transition, and chronic immune activation coupled to energy metabolism. Uses ODE and stochastic frameworks to represent reduced NK cytotoxicity and altered cytokine profiles.

chapters.title: Neuroendocrine and Autonomic Models
chapters.about: Develops mathematical models of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis, the autonomic nervous system, and sleep-wake regulation, emphasizing bidirectional coupling with the immune and metabolic systems. Models HPA axis dysfunction through enhanced negative feedback sensitivity, reduced circadian amplitude, and altered stress responsiveness.

chapters.title: Integrated Multi-System Models
chapters.about: Formalizes the inter-system couplings among energy metabolism, immune function, neuroendocrine regulation, and autonomic control to construct an integrated model. Centers on the bidirectional energy-immune feedback loop and hypothesizes that this coupled system is bistable with healthy and disease attractors.

chapters.title: Temporal Evolution and Disease Trajectories
chapters.about: Extends the subsystem models to longer timescales, covering disease onset, symptom fluctuations, disease progression, and treatment response. Develops tipping point dynamics based on crossing a state-space separatrix versus a recovery-failure model of accumulated damage, and traces a consolidated infection-to-onset cascade.

chapters.title: Predictive Applications and Clinical Translation
chapters.about: Examines how the mathematical models translate into practical clinical applications, including personalized pacing optimization, activity planning algorithms, real-time monitoring integration, and severity-stratified monitoring. Assesses each application’s current feasibility and barriers.

chapters.title: Formal Causal Hierarchy Analysis
chapters.about: Encodes the qualitative causal hierarchy into formal mathematical models. Develops a coupled ODE system tracking Complex I function, safe mode activation, pro-inflammatory cytokines, viral load, threat signals, and methylation, analyzing the epigenetic consolidation treatment, compartment bistability, and the timescale hierarchy constraining therapeutic sequencing.
